# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs

## Overview

Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by understanding the current project context, then ask questions one at a time to refine the idea. Once you understand what you're building, present the design and get user approval.

<HARD-GATE>
Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. This applies to EVERY project regardless of perceived simplicity.
</HARD-GATE>

## Anti-Pattern: "This Is Too Simple To Need A Design"

Every project goes through this process. A todo list, a single-function utility, a config change — all of them. "Simple" projects are where unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work. The design can be short (a few sentences for truly simple projects), but you MUST present it and get approval.

## Checklist

You MUST create a task for each of these items and complete them in order:

1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria
3. **Propose 2-3 approaches** — with trade-offs and your recommendation
4. **Present design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section
5. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit
6. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan

## Process Flow

```dot
digraph brainstorming {
    "Explore project context" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions" [shape=box];
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" [shape=box];
    "Present design sections" [shape=box];
    "User approves design?" [shape=diamond];
    "Write design doc" [shape=box];
    "Invoke writing-plans skill" [shape=doublecircle];

    "Explore project context" -> "Ask clarifying questions";
    "Ask clarifying questions" -> "Propose 2-3 approaches";
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" -> "Present design sections";
    "Present design sections" -> "User approves design?";
    "User approves design?" -> "Present design sections" [label="no, revise"];
    "User approves design?" -> "Write design doc" [label="yes"];
    "Write design doc" -> "Invoke writing-plans skill";
}
```

**The terminal state is invoking writing-plans.** Do NOT invoke frontend-design, mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. The ONLY skill you invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans.

## The Process

**Understanding the idea:**
- Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)
- Ask questions one at a time to refine the idea
- Prefer multiple choice questions when possible, but open-ended is fine too
- Only one question per message - if a topic needs more exploration, break it into multiple questions
- Focus on understanding: purpose, constraints, success criteria

**Exploring approaches:**
- Propose 2-3 different approaches with trade-offs
- Present options conversationally with your recommendation and reasoning
- Lead with your recommended option and explain why

**Presenting the design:**
- Once you believe you understand what you're building, present the design
- Scale each section to its complexity: a few sentences if straightforward, up to 200-300 words if nuanced
- Ask after each section whether it looks right so far
- Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing
- Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn't make sense

## After the Design

**Documentation:**
- Write the validated design to `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`
- Use elements-of-style:writing-clearly-and-concisely skill if available
- Commit the design document to git

**Implementation:**
- Invoke the writing-plans skill to create a detailed implementation plan
- Do NOT invoke any other skill. writing-plans is the next step.

## Key Principles

- **One question at a time** - Don't overwhelm with multiple questions
- **Multiple choice preferred** - Easier to answer than open-ended when possible
- **YAGNI ruthlessly** - Remove unnecessary features from all designs
- **Explore alternatives** - Always propose 2-3 approaches before settling
- **Incremental validation** - Present design, get approval before moving on
- **Be flexible** - Go back and clarify when something doesn't make sense

1→# DuckDB Data Agent
     2→
     3→> **Note:** This project is built with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code)(using Opus 4.6 and [superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers)) by more than 95% and human-reviewed by author.
     4→
     5→[![Deploy to Render](https://render.com/images/deploy-to-render-button.svg)](https://render.com/deploy)
     6→
     7→A SQL playground with an AI-powered data analysis agent. Upload CSV files, write SQL queries, or ask questions in plain English — powered by [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) on a lightweight [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) backend with a React frontend.
     8→
     9→## Features
    10→
    11→### General
    12→
    13→- **Dark / light mode** — Toggle between dark and light themes with the sun/moon button in the header; respects your OS preference on first visit and remembers your choice across sessions
    14→
    15→### SQL Playground
    16→
    17→- **DuckDB SQL engine** — Fast, in-process analytical database on the backend
    18→- **CSV file upload** — Drag-and-drop or click to import CSV files (up to 500 MB) with automatic schema detection
    19→- **Sample dataset** — One-click load of the Titanic dataset to get started quickly
    20→- **SQL query editor** — Write and execute queries with Ctrl/Cmd+Enter
    21→- **Interactive results** — Sortable columns, per-column filters, and global search across results
    22→- **EXPLAIN support** — Markdown-rendered output for `EXPLAIN` and `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` queries
    23→- **Table sidebar** — Collapsible panel to browse tables, inspect columns, and view types
    24→
    25→### AI Agent
    26→
    27→- **Natural language queries** — Ask questions about your data in plain English; the agent writes and executes SQL for you
    28→- **Streaming responses** — Real-time token streaming powered by Claude via the [Anthropic Agent SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python)
    29→- **Visible reasoning** — Collapsible thinking block shows the agent's intermediate steps and SQL queries
    30→- **Inline results** — Query results rendered inline within the conversation
    31→- **Edit & delete messages** — Hover over any user message to edit or delete it; editing re-sends the modified query with prior conversation as context, deleting rewinds the conversation to that point
    32→- **Privacy-conscious** — Requires an Anthropic API key stored in a server-side `.env` file; your data and key are never sent anywhere besides the Anthropic API
    33→- **Langfuse observability** (optional) — Built-in [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/) tracing for monitoring agent interactions, with a one-click dashboard link in the UI
    34→
    35→## Getting Started
    36→
    37→### Prerequisites
    38→
    39→- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 20+
    40→- [Python](https://www.python.org/) 3.12+
    41→- [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/)
    42→
    43→### Installation
    44→
    45→```bash
    46→make install
    47→```
    48→
    49→Or install frontend and backend separately:
    50→
    51→```bash
    52→cd frontend && npm install
    53→cd backend && poetry install
    54→```
    55→
    56→### Configuration
    57→
    58→Copy the example environment file and add your Anthropic API key:
    59→
    60→```bash
    61→cp backend/.env.example backend/.env
    62→```
    63→
    64→Edit `backend/.env` and set your key:
    65→
    66→```
    67→ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
    68→ANTHROPIC_MODEL=sonnet    # optional, defaults to sonnet
    69→```
    70→
    71→> Both variables are only needed for the AI agent. The SQL playground works without them, but both require the backend running.
    72→
    73→#### Langfuse (optional)
    74→
    75→To enable agent tracing with [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/), add these to `backend/.env`:
    76→
    77→```
    78→LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-...
    79→LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-...
    80→LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com   # optional, defaults to cloud
    81→```
    82→
    83→When configured, every agent conversation is traced (LLM turns, tool calls, SQL execution) and a **Langfuse Traces** button appears in the agent panel header linking to your dashboard. When not configured, tracing is disabled with zero overhead.
    84→
    85→### Development
    86→
    87→Start both the frontend and backend:
    88→
    89→```bash
    90→make dev
    91→```
    92→
    93→Or run them separately:
    94→
    95→```bash
    96→make frontend   # http://localhost:5173
    97→make backend    # http://localhost:8000
    98→```
    99→
   100→Open http://localhost:5173 to use the app. The Vite dev server proxies `/api` requests to the backend automatically.
   101→
   102→## Production Build and Deployment
   103→
   104→The project ships as a single Docker image that bundles the React frontend and FastAPI backend. A multi-stage `Dockerfile` builds the frontend, then copies the output into the backend's static directory.
   105→
   106→### Build and run locally
   107→
   108→```bash
   109→docker build -t duckdb-data-agent .
   110→docker run -p 10000:10000 \
   111→  -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... \
   112→  -e LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-... \
   113→  -e LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-... \
   114→  duckdb-data-agent
   115→```
   116→
   117→Open http://localhost:10000 to use the app.
   118→
   119→### Deploy to Render
   120→
   121→A `render.yaml` is included for one-click deployment on [Render](https://render.com/):
   122→
   123→1. Push this repo to GitHub.
   124→2. In Render, create a new **Blueprint** and connect the repo.
   125→3. Set the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable in the Render dashboard. Optionally set `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` to override the default model (`sonnet`). To enable Langfuse tracing, also set `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY` and `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY`.
   126→
   127→Render will build the Docker image and deploy it automatically on every push to `main`.
   128→
   129→## Project Structure
   130→
   131→```
   132→├── frontend/               # React frontend
   133→│   ├── public/             #   Static assets (Langfuse icon)
   134→│   ├── src/
   135→│   │   ├── components/     #   UI components (editor, results, sidebar, chat)
   136→│   │   ├── agent/          #   Agent service (SSE event handling)
   137→│   │   ├── AgentContext.tsx #   Agent state management
   138→│   │   ├── ThemeContext.tsx #   Dark/light theme state & persistence
   139→│   │   └── types.ts        #   Shared TypeScript interfaces
   140→│   ├── index.html          #   HTML entry point
   141→│   ├── package.json        #   npm config
   142→│   └── vite.config.ts      #   Vite bundler config
   143→├── backend/                # FastAPI backend
   144→│   └── app/
   145→│       ├── main.py         #   App setup & CORS
   146→│       ├── config.py       #   Environment variables (API key, model)
   147→│       ├── database.py     #   DuckDB connection & query execution
   148→│       ├── agent.py        #   Agent loop & SSE streaming
   149→│       ├── tracing.py      #   Langfuse client wrapper & initialization
   150→│       ├── tools.py        #   Agent SDK tool definitions (execute_sql)
   151→│       ├── data/           #   Sample datasets (titanic.csv)
   152→│       └── routes/         #   API endpoints (tables, query, chat, langfuse status)
   153→├── Dockerfile              # Multi-stage production build
   154→├── render.yaml             # Render deployment config
   155→└── Makefile                # Dev commands (install, dev, clean)
   156→```
   157→
   158→## Tech Stack
   159→
   160→**Frontend**
   161→- [React](https://react.dev/) 18 + [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)
   162→- [Vite](https://vite.dev/)
   163→
   164→**Backend**
   165→- [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) + [Uvicorn](https://www.uvicorn.org/)
   166→- [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) (Python)
   167→- [Anthropic Agent SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python)
   168→- [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/) (optional, for observability)
   169→
   170→## License
   171→
   172→[MIT](LICENSE.txt)
   173→

1→from fastapi import APIRouter
     2→from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
     3→from pydantic import BaseModel
     4→
     5→from app.agent import stream_chat
     6→
     7→router = APIRouter(prefix="/api", tags=["chat"])
     8→
     9→
    10→class ChatRequest(BaseModel):
    11→    message: str
    12→    session_id: str | None = None
    13→
    14→
    15→class ChatEditRequest(BaseModel):
    16→    new_message: str
    17→    conversation_history: list[dict] = []
    18→
    19→
    20→@router.post("/chat")
    21→async def chat(request: ChatRequest):
    22→    return StreamingResponse(
    23→        stream_chat(request.message, request.session_id),
    24→        media_type="text/event-stream",
    25→        headers={
    26→            "Cache-Control": "no-cache",
    27→            "Connection": "keep-alive",
    28→            "X-Accel-Buffering": "no",
    29→        },
    30→    )
    31→
    32→
    33→@router.post("/chat/edit")
    34→async def chat_edit(request: ChatEditRequest):
    35→    """Edit a message: start a fresh session with conversation history as context."""
    36→    return StreamingResponse(
    37→        stream_chat(
    38→            request.new_message,
    39→            session_id=None,
    40→            conversation_history=request.conversation_history,
    41→        ),
    42→        media_type="text/event-stream",
    43→        headers={
    44→            "Cache-Control": "no-cache",
    45→            "Connection": "keep-alive",
    46→            "X-Accel-Buffering": "no",
    47→        },

## Project Exploration Report: DuckDB Data Agent

Based on my thorough exploration of the project, here are all the findings:

---

### 1. **What is this project?**

**DuckDB Data Agent** is a full-stack SQL playground with an AI-powered data analysis agent. It allows users to:
- Upload CSV files and write SQL queries directly
- Ask natural language questions about data that an AI agent answers by writing and executing SQL
- Inspect table structures and query results with interactive features
- Toggle between a SQL editor mode and an AI agent chat mode

The project is built with React 18 + TypeScript on the frontend and FastAPI + DuckDB on the backend. According to the README, it was built by Claude Code (Opus 4.6) with human review.

---

### 2. **Tech Stack**

**Frontend:**
- React 18.3.1 + TypeScript (~5.6.2)
- Vite 5.4.10 (build tool with dev server proxy to backend)
- react-markdown 10.1.0 (for rendering markdown output)
- remark-gfm 4.0.1 (for GitHub-flavored markdown)
- ESLint for linting

**Backend:**
- FastAPI 0.129.0 (web framework)
- Uvicorn 0.41.0 (ASGI server)
- DuckDB 1.4.4 (in-process SQL engine)
- python-dotenv 1.2.1 (environment variable management)
- claude-agent-sdk 0.1.38 (Anthropic Agent SDK for streaming LLM responses)
- Langfuse 3.0.0 (optional observability/tracing)
- langsmith (optional observability integration)

**Build & Deployment:**
- Multi-stage Docker build (bundles React frontend + FastAPI backend)
- Render.yaml for one-click deployment to Render platform
- Makefile for local development commands

---

### 3. **File/Folder Structure**

```
/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/
├── frontend/                           # React frontend
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── components/                 # UI components
│   │   │   ├── AgentPanel.tsx/.css     # AI chat interface
│   │   │   ├── ChatInput.tsx/.css      # Chat message input
│   │   │   ├── ErrorMessage.tsx/.css   # Error display
│   │   │   ├── FileUpload.tsx/.css     # CSV upload & sample load
│   │   │   ├── InlineQueryResult.tsx/.css # Tool call results display
│   │   │   ├── MessageBubble.tsx/.css  # Chat message bubbles
│   │   │   ├── QueryEditor.tsx/.css    # SQL editor textarea
│   │   │   ├── ResultMarkdown.tsx/.css # EXPLAIN markdown output
│   │   │   ├── ResultsTable.tsx/.css   # Interactive results table
│   │   │   └── Sidebar.tsx/.css        # Table browser sidebar
│   │   ├── agent/
│   │   │   └── agentService.ts         # SSE streaming and event handling
│   │   ├── AgentContext.tsx            # Agent state management
│   │   ├── ThemeContext.tsx            # Dark/light theme state
│   │   ├── App.tsx                     # Main app component
│   │   ├── App.css                     # App layout styles
│   │   ├── index.css                   # Global styles + theme CSS variables
│   │   ├── types.ts                    # TypeScript interfaces
│   │   ├── useAgent.ts                 # Custom hook for agent context
│   │   └── main.tsx                    # React entry point
│   ├── index.html                      # HTML entry point
│   ├── vite.config.ts                  # Vite bundler config
│   └── package.json
├── backend/                            # FastAPI backend
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── routes/
│   │   │   ├── chat.py                 # SSE chat endpoint (/api/chat, /api/chat/edit)
│   │   │   ├── langfuse_status.py      # Langfuse config status
│   │   │   ├── query.py                # SQL execution endpoint (/api/query)
│   │   │   └── tables.py               # Table management endpoints
│   │   ├── agent.py                    # Agent loop with streaming
│   │   ├── config.py                   # Environment variables
│   │   ├── database.py                 # DuckDB connection & queries
│   │   ├── main.py                     # FastAPI app setup
│   │   ├── tools.py                    # Agent SDK tool definitions
│   │   ├── tracing.py                  # Langfuse client integration
│   │   └── data/                       # Sample datasets (titanic.csv)
│   └── pyproject.toml
├── Dockerfile                          # Multi-stage production build
├── Makefile                            # Development commands
├── README.md                           # Project documentation
├── render.yaml                         # Render deployment config
└── LICENSE.txt
```

---

### 4. **Frontend Organization**

**Routing & Layout:**
- **Single Page Application (SPA)** - No traditional routing library (no React Router)
- Layout is two-mode: Editor Mode vs Agent Mode (toggled by button)
- Editor Mode: Sidebar (tables) | Main area (upload, SQL editor, results)
- Agent Mode: Full-width chat interface with thinking/tool visibility

**Components Hierarchy:**
```
App
├── AppContent (uses ThemeContext, AgentContext)
│   ├── Sidebar (tables list, collapse toggle)
│   ├── Header (title, theme toggle, mode toggle)
│   └── Conditional (Editor OR Agent)
│       └── Editor Mode:
│           ├── FileUpload
│           ├── QueryEditor
│           ├── ErrorMessage
│           └── ResultsTable or ResultMarkdown
│       └── Agent Mode:
│           ├── AgentPanel
│               ├── MessageBubble (repeating for each message)
│               │   └── ThinkingBlock (collapsible details)
│               │   └── InlineQueryResult (for tool calls)
│               └── ChatInput
```

**State Management:**
- **AgentContext**: Chat messages, streaming state, send/edit/delete/clear functions
- **ThemeContext**: Current theme ('light' or 'dark'), toggleTheme function
- No Redux/Zustand - just React Context API

---

### 5. **Dark/Light Mode Toggle Implementation**

**ThemeContext.tsx** (file: `/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/frontend/src/ThemeContext.tsx`)
- Uses React Context API with useState
- Reads initial theme from `localStorage` or OS preference via `window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')`
- Sets `data-theme` attribute on `document.documentElement`
- Persists choice to localStorage

**CSS Theme Variables** (file: `/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/frontend/src/index.css`)
- Light theme is the default (`:root` selector)
- Dark theme uses `[data-theme="dark"]` selector
- **58 CSS custom properties** including:
  - Background colors (primary, secondary, tertiary, code, hover, user messages)
  - Text colors (primary, secondary, tertiary, code, muted, subtle, disabled, faint)
  - Border colors (faint, light, medium, dark, dashed)
  - Accent colors (primary indigo, secondary blue)
  - Error, success, and tool-specific colors

**Toggle Button** (file: `/Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent/frontend/src/App.tsx`, lines 117-133)
- Sun icon when in dark mode
- Moon icon when in light mode
- Located in app header
- aria-label: `"Switch to light mode"` (dark) or `"Switch to dark mode"` (light)

---

### 6. **Hardcoded Text/Strings in UI**

**App.tsx:**
- "DuckDB Data Agent" (page title)
- "Editor Mode" / "Agent Mode" (button text)
- "Switch to light mode" / "Switch to dark mode" (aria-label, title)

**FileUpload.tsx:**
- "Only .csv files are supported." (alert)
- "File exceeds 500MB limit." (alert)
- "Uploading..." (while uploading)
- "Drop a CSV file here or click to browse" (instruction)
- "or" (divider text)
- "Loading..." / "Load Sample Dataset (Titanic)" (button)

**QueryEditor.tsx:**
- "Enter SQL query... (Ctrl+Enter to run)" (placeholder)
- "Running..." / "Run Query" (button text)

**Sidebar.tsx:**
- "Tables" (sidebar header)
- "No tables yet. Upload a CSV to get started." (empty state)
- "Expand sidebar" / "Collapse sidebar" (aria-label)
- "Delete table {tableName}" (title attribute)
- Delete table label in aria-label

**AgentPanel.tsx:**
- "Agent Mode" (panel header)
- "Langfuse Traces" (button)
- "Open Langfuse dashboard" (title when enabled)
- "Langfuse not configured" (title when disabled)
- "Clear" (button)
- "Ask a question about your data, and the agent will write and run SQL queries to find the answer." (empty state message)

**ChatInput.tsx:**
- "Waiting for response..." / "Ask about your data..." (placeholder)
- "Send" (button)

**MessageBubble.tsx:**
- "You" / "Assistant" (message author)
- "Thinking..." (label for thinking block)
- "Delete this and all following messages?" (confirmation dialog)
- "Delete" / "Cancel" (confirmation buttons)
- "Edit message" / "Delete message" (title attributes)
- "Save & Resend" / "Cancel" (edit mode buttons)
- "Answer" (segment label)

**ResultsTable.tsx:**
- "Search all columns…" (global search placeholder)
- "Filter…" (column filter placeholder)
- "{rows} row(s)" / "{rows} of {rowCount} rows" (summary)
- "(showing first {DISPLAY_CAP})" (truncation message)

**ResultMarkdown.tsx:**
- "{rowCount} row(s)" (summary)

**InlineQueryResult.tsx:**
- "SQL Query" / "Bash" / "Read File" / "Write File" / "Edit File" (tool names)
- "Executing..." (pending state)
- "{rowCount} row(s)" / "(showing {MAX_DISPLAY_ROWS})" (result metadata)

**index.html:**
- "DuckDB Data Agent" (page title in `<title>`)

---

### 7. **i18n and Localization**

**No i18n/localization infrastructure exists.** I searched for:
- No `i18n` directory or config file
- No localization/translation libraries (no react-intl, i18next, etc.)
- No locale/translation JSON files
- No language selector in the UI
- No environment variables for locale settings

**Current state:**
- All text is hardcoded in English in the source code
- All CSS is hardcoded with no localization considerations
- No translation strings extracted or separated from components

---

| **Project Type** | Full-stack AI-powered SQL playground |
| **Frontend** | React 18 + TypeScript, Vite, Context API for state |
| **Backend** | FastAPI + DuckDB, Anthropic Agent SDK, Langfuse optional |

Now let me present the approach. Since the answers already converge on a clear direction, here are the approaches:

## Approach Comparison

### Approach A: Custom Context + JSON files (Recommended)

- Create a `LanguageContext` similar to the existing `ThemeContext`
- Translation files: `frontend/src/i18n/en.json` and `frontend/src/i18n/zh-TW.json`
- Custom `useTranslation()` hook returns a `t(key)` function
- Detection: check localStorage first, then `navigator.language`, fallback to `en`
- Toggle: text label button (EN/中) in header, left of theme toggle
- **Zero new dependencies**
- Mirrors the existing ThemeContext pattern perfectly

### Approach B: react-i18next

- Install `i18next` + `react-i18next` + `i18next-browser-languagedetector`
- Same JSON files but managed through i18next's config
- More powerful (pluralization, interpolation, namespaces)
- **3 new dependencies for ~25 strings** - overkill

### Approach C: Compile-time approach (e.g. typesafe-i18n)

- Type-safe keys at build time
- More complex setup, Vite plugin needed
- Overkill for 2 languages and ~25 strings

**Recommendation: Approach A.** It mirrors the existing ThemeContext pattern, adds zero dependencies, and is perfectly sized for ~25 strings across 2 languages.

## Design Section 3: Data Flow & Edge Cases

**Data flow:**
```
User clicks toggle → setLanguage('zh-TW') → localStorage updated

- No number/date formatting (the app uses raw SQL output)
- No plural rules (we use simple `{count} row(s)` pattern in both languages)
- No namespacing (only ~40 keys total)
- No lazy loading of translations (both files are tiny)

# i18n Design: English + Traditional Chinese

**Date:** 2026-02-20
**Scope:** Frontend UI strings only (not AI agent responses)
**Languages:** English (`en`), Traditional Chinese (`zh-TW`)

## Approach

Custom React Context + JSON translation files. Zero new dependencies. Mirrors the existing `ThemeContext` pattern.

## Architecture

### New Files

- `frontend/src/i18n/en.json` — English translation strings
- `frontend/src/i18n/zh-TW.json` — Traditional Chinese translation strings
- `frontend/src/LanguageContext.tsx` — Language state, provider, and `useTranslation` hook

### Modified Files

- `frontend/src/App.tsx` — Wrap with `LanguageProvider`, add language toggle in header
- All component files — Replace hardcoded strings with `t('key')` calls

### Language Detection Priority

1. `localStorage.getItem('language')` (user's saved preference)
2. `navigator.language` — if starts with `zh`, use `zh-TW`; otherwise `en`
3. Fallback: `en`

### LanguageContext API

```typescript
type Language = 'en' | 'zh-TW';

interface LanguageContextType {
  language: Language;
  setLanguage: (lang: Language) => void;
  t: (key: string, params?: Record<string, string | number>) => string;
}
```

The `t()` function:
- Looks up the key in the current language's translation file
- Supports simple interpolation: `t('rows', { count: 5 })` replaces `{count}` in the string
- Falls back to returning the key itself if not found

## UI Toggle

- **Position:** Header, immediately left of the sun/moon theme toggle
- **Style:** Same button styling as theme toggle
- **Label:** Shows `EN` when in English, `中` when in Traditional Chinese
- **Behavior:** Click toggles between the two languages
- **Accessibility:** `aria-label` of "Switch to 中文" / "Switch to English"

## Translation Keys

~40 flat key-value pairs covering: app title, mode labels, upload text, query editor placeholders, sidebar labels, agent panel text, chat input, message bubbles, results table, tool names, confirmation dialogs, error messages.

Both language files use identical keys.

## Data Flow

```
User clicks toggle → setLanguage('zh-TW') → localStorage updated
→ LanguageContext re-renders → all t() calls return new language strings
→ UI updates instantly (no page reload)
→ document.documentElement.lang updated for accessibility
```

## Edge Cases

- **Invalid localStorage value:** Falls back to OS detection, then `en`
- **OS language not zh or en:** Defaults to `en`
- **Missing translation key:** Returns the key itself (non-breaking fallback)
- **HTML `lang` attribute:** Updated on `<html>` element when language changes

## Out of Scope (YAGNI)

- RTL support (neither language needs it)
- Number/date formatting (app uses raw SQL output)
- Plural rules (using `{count} row(s)` pattern)
- Namespacing (only ~40 keys)
- Lazy loading of translations (files are tiny)
- Backend/agent translation (excluded per design decision)

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** This should be run in a dedicated worktree (created by brainstorming skill).

**Save plans to:** `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For Claude:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

**Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

**Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

**Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

**Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## Remember
- Exact file paths always
- Complete code in plan (not "add validation")
- Exact commands with expected output
- Reference relevant skills with @ syntax
- DRY, YAGNI, TDD, frequent commits

## Execution Handoff

After saving the plan, offer execution choice:

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/plans/<filename>.md`. Two execution options:**

**1. Subagent-Driven (this session)** - I dispatch fresh subagent per task, review between tasks, fast iteration

**2. Parallel Session (separate)** - Open new session with executing-plans, batch execution with checkpoints

**Which approach?"**

**If Subagent-Driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development
- Stay in this session
- Fresh subagent per task + code review

**If Parallel Session chosen:**
- Guide them to open new session in worktree
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** New session uses superpowers:executing-plans

- All component files — Replace hardcoded strings with `t('key')` calls

### Language Detection Priority

1. `localStorage.getItem('language')` (user's saved preference)
2. `navigator.language` — if starts with `zh`, use `zh-TW`; otherwise `en`
3. Fallback: `en`

### LanguageContext API

```typescript
type Language = 'en' | 'zh-TW';

interface LanguageContextType {
  language: Language;
  setLanguage: (lang: Language) => void;
  t: (key: string, params?: Record<string, string | number>) => string;
}
```

The `t()` function:
- Looks up the key in the current language's translation file
- Supports simple interpolation: `t('rows', { count: 5 })` replaces `{count}` in the string
- Falls back to returning the key itself if not found

## UI Toggle

- **Position:** Header, immediately left of the sun/moon theme toggle
- **Style:** Same button styling as theme toggle
- **Label:** Shows `EN` when in English, `中` when in Traditional Chinese
- **Behavior:** Click toggles between the two languages
- **Accessibility:** `aria-label` of "Switch to 中文" / "Switch to English"

## Translation Keys

~40 flat key-value pairs covering: app title, mode labels, upload text, query editor placeholders, sidebar labels, agent panel text, chat input, message bubbles, results table, tool names, confirmation dialogs, error messages.

Both language files use identical keys.

## Data Flow

```
User clicks toggle → setLanguage('zh-TW') → localStorage updated
→ LanguageContext re-renders → all t() calls return new language strings
→ UI updates instantly (no page reload)
→ document.documentElement.lang updated for accessibility
```

## Edge Cases

- **Invalid localStorage value:** Falls back to OS detection, then `en`
- **OS language not zh or en:** Defaults to `en`
- **Missing translation key:** Returns the key itself (non-breaking fallback)
- **HTML `lang` attribute:** Updated on `<html>` element when language changes

## Out of Scope (YAGNI)

- RTL support (neither language needs it)
- Number/date formatting (app uses raw SQL output)
- Plural rules (using `{count} row(s)` pattern)
- Namespacing (only ~40 keys)
- Lazy loading of translations (files are tiny)
- Backend/agent translation (excluded per design decision)

## Prompt Templates

- `./implementer-prompt.md` - Dispatch implementer subagent
- `./spec-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch spec compliance reviewer subagent
- `./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent

## Example Workflow

```

[Read plan file once: docs/plans/feature-plan.md]
[Extract all 5 tasks with full text and context]
[Create TodoWrite with all tasks]

[Get Task 1 text and context (already extracted)]
[Dispatch implementation subagent with full task text + context]

Implementer: "Before I begin - should the hook be installed at user or system level?"

You: "User level (~/.config/superpowers/hooks/)"

Implementer: "Got it. Implementing now..."
[Later] Implementer:
  - Implemented install-hook command
  - Added tests, 5/5 passing
  - Self-review: Found I missed --force flag, added it
  - Committed

[Dispatch spec compliance reviewer]
Spec reviewer: ✅ Spec compliant - all requirements met, nothing extra

[Get git SHAs, dispatch code quality reviewer]

[Mark Task 1 complete]

Task 2: Recovery modes

[Get Task 2 text and context (already extracted)]
[Dispatch implementation subagent with full task text + context]

  - Added verify/repair modes
  - 8/8 tests passing
  - Self-review: All good
  - Committed

[Dispatch spec compliance reviewer]
Spec reviewer: ❌ Issues:
  - Missing: Progress reporting (spec says "report every 100 items")
  - Extra: Added --json flag (not requested)

[Implementer fixes issues]
Implementer: Removed --json flag, added progress reporting

[Spec reviewer reviews again]
Spec reviewer: ✅ Spec compliant now

[Dispatch code quality reviewer]

...

[After all tasks]

```

## Advantages

**vs. Manual execution:**
- Subagents follow TDD naturally
- Fresh context per task (no confusion)
- Parallel-safe (subagents don't interfere)
- Subagent can ask questions (before AND during work)

**vs. Executing Plans:**
- Same session (no handoff)
- Continuous progress (no waiting)
- Review checkpoints automatic

**Efficiency gains:**
- No file reading overhead (controller provides full text)
- Controller curates exactly what context is needed
- Subagent gets complete information upfront
- Questions surfaced before work begins (not after)

**Quality gates:**
- Self-review catches issues before handoff
- Two-stage review: spec compliance, then code quality
- Review loops ensure fixes actually work
- Spec compliance prevents over/under-building
- Code quality ensures implementation is well-built

**Cost:**
- More subagent invocations (implementer + 2 reviewers per task)
- Controller does more prep work (extracting all tasks upfront)
- Review loops add iterations
- But catches issues early (cheaper than debugging later)

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent
- Skip reviews (spec compliance OR code quality)
- Proceed with unfixed issues
- Dispatch multiple implementation subagents in parallel (conflicts)
- Make subagent read plan file (provide full text instead)
- Skip scene-setting context (subagent needs to understand where task fits)
- Ignore subagent questions (answer before letting them proceed)
- Accept "close enough" on spec compliance (spec reviewer found issues = not done)
- Skip review loops (reviewer found issues = implementer fixes = review again)
- Let implementer self-review replace actual review (both are needed)
- **Start code quality review before spec compliance is ✅** (wrong order)
- Move to next task while either review has open issues

**If subagent asks questions:**
- Answer clearly and completely
- Provide additional context if needed
- Don't rush them into implementation

**If reviewer finds issues:**
- Implementer (same subagent) fixes them
- Reviewer reviews again
- Repeat until approved
- Don't skip the re-review

**If subagent fails task:**
- Dispatch fix subagent with specific instructions
- Don't try to fix manually (context pollution)

## Integration

**Required workflow skills:**
- **superpowers:using-git-worktrees** - REQUIRED: Set up isolated workspace before starting
- **superpowers:writing-plans** - Creates the plan this skill executes
- **superpowers:requesting-code-review** - Code review template for reviewer subagents
- **superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch** - Complete development after all tasks

**Subagents should use:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - Subagents follow TDD for each task

**Alternative workflow:**
- **superpowers:executing-plans** - Use for parallel session instead of same-session execution

Task tool (general-purpose):

    **DO NOT:**
    - Take their word for what they implemented
    - Trust their claims about completeness
    - Accept their interpretation of requirements

    - Read the actual code they wrote
    - Compare actual implementation to requirements line by line

    - Look for extra features they didn't mention

    **Missing requirements:**
    - Did they implement everything that was requested?
    - Are there requirements they skipped or missed?
    - Did they claim something works but didn't actually implement it?

    **Extra/unneeded work:**
    - Did they build things that weren't requested?
    - Did they over-engineer or add unnecessary features?
    - Did they add "nice to haves" that weren't in spec?

    **Misunderstandings:**
    - Did they interpret requirements differently than intended?
    - Did they solve the wrong problem?
    - Did they implement the right feature but wrong way?

    **Verify by reading code, not by trusting report.**

    Report:
    - ✅ Spec compliant (if everything matches after code inspection)
    - ❌ Issues found: [list specifically what's missing or extra, with file:line references]

You are implementing Tasks 5-13: Translate all 9 components to use the i18n system. ## Context The i18n system is already set up: - `frontend/src/LanguageContext.tsx` exports `useTranslation()` which returns `{ language, setLanguage, t }` - `t(key)` returns the translated string, `t(key, { param: value })` supports interpolation - Translation files are at `frontend/src/i18n/en.json` and `frontend/src/i18n/zh-TW.json` Your job is to replace ALL hardcoded English strings in each component with `t('key')` calls. For each component: 1. Add `import { useTranslation } from '../LanguageContext';` 2. Add `const { t } = useTranslation();` inside the component function 3. Replace every hardcoded string with the appropriate `t()` call ## Available translation keys (from en.json): ``` appTitle, editorMode, agentMode, switchToLight, switchToDark, switchToZh, switchToEn, connectingToBackend, failedToConnect, uploadDropText, uploadOr, loadSample, loading, uploading, csvOnly, fileTooLarge, queryPlaceholder, runQuery, running, tablesHeader, noTables, expandSidebar, collapseSidebar, deleteTable, deleteTableConfirm, rowCount, agentHeader, langfuseTraces, openLangfuse, langfuseNotConfigured, clear, agentEmptyState, chatPlaceholderWaiting, chatPlaceholder, send, you, assistant, thinking, thinkingLabel, answer, deleteConfirm, delete, cancel, editMessage, deleteMessage, saveResend, searchColumns, filterPlaceholder, rowsOf, showingFirst, sqlQuery, bash, readFile, writeFile, editFile, executing, rowCountInTime, rowsFilteredInTime, showingCount ``` ## Component-by-component instructions: ### 1. FileUpload.tsx (`frontend/src/components/FileUpload.tsx`) Replace: - `alert('Only .csv files are supported.');` → `alert(t('csvOnly'));` - `alert('File exceeds 500MB limit.');` → `alert(t('fileTooLarge'));` - `

Uploading...

` → `

{t('uploading')}

` - `Drop a CSV file here or click to browse` → `{t('uploadDropText')}` - `or` → `{t('uploadOr')}` - `{loadingSample ? 'Loading...' : 'Load Sample Dataset (Titanic)'}` → `{loadingSample ? t('loading') : t('loadSample')}` ### 2. QueryEditor.tsx (`frontend/src/components/QueryEditor.tsx`) Replace: - `placeholder="Enter SQL query... (Ctrl+Enter to run)"` → `placeholder={t('queryPlaceholder')}` - `{running ? 'Running...' : 'Run Query'}` → `{running ? t('running') : t('runQuery')}` ### 3. Sidebar.tsx (`frontend/src/components/Sidebar.tsx`) Replace: - `

Tables

` → `

{t('tablesHeader')}

` - `aria-label={collapsed ? 'Expand sidebar' : 'Collapse sidebar'}` → `aria-label={collapsed ? t('expandSidebar') : t('collapseSidebar')}` - `No tables yet. Upload a CSV to get started.` → `{t('noTables')}` - `{table.rowCount} row{table.rowCount !== 1 ? 's' : ''}` → `{t('rowCount', { count: table.rowCount })}` - `` title={`Delete table "${table.name}"`} `` → `title={t('deleteTable', { name: table.name })}` - `` aria-label={`Delete table ${table.name}`} `` → `aria-label={t('deleteTable', { name: table.name })}` ### 4. AgentPanel.tsx (`frontend/src/components/AgentPanel.tsx`) Replace: - `Agent Mode` → `{t('agentHeader')}` - `title={langfuseStatus.enabled ? 'Open Langfuse dashboard' : 'Langfuse not configured'}` → `title={langfuseStatus.enabled ? t('openLangfuse') : t('langfuseNotConfigured')}` - `Langfuse Traces` → `{t('langfuseTraces')}` - `Clear` → `{t('clear')}` - The empty state text `Ask a question about your data...` → `{t('agentEmptyState')}` ### 5. ChatInput.tsx (`frontend/src/components/ChatInput.tsx`) Replace: - `placeholder={isStreaming ? 'Waiting for response...' : 'Ask about your data...'}` → `placeholder={isStreaming ? t('chatPlaceholderWaiting') : t('chatPlaceholder')}` - `Send` → `{t('send')}` ### 6. MessageBubble.tsx (`frontend/src/components/MessageBubble.tsx`) This one is more complex. Both `ThinkingBlock` and `MessageBubble` need `useTranslation`. For the standalone function `getLastThinkingLine`, it returns `'Thinking...'` as a fallback. Change its signature to accept a `t` parameter: ```typescript function getLastThinkingLine(segments: ContentSegment[], streamingRemainder: string | undefined, t: (key: string) => string): string { ``` And change the last `return 'Thinking...';` to `return t('thinking');` In `ThinkingBlock`: - Add `const { t } = useTranslation();` - Update the call: `const summary = getLastThinkingLine(segments, streamingRemainder, t);` - `Thinking` → `{t('thinkingLabel')}` In `MessageBubble`: - Add `const { t } = useTranslation();` - `{isUser ? 'You' : 'Assistant'}` → `{isUser ? t('you') : t('assistant')}` - `title="Edit message"` → `title={t('editMessage')}` - `title="Delete message"` → `title={t('deleteMessage')}` - `Delete this and all following messages?` → `{t('deleteConfirm')}` - The delete confirm button `Delete` → `{t('delete')}` - The cancel button `Cancel` (two places) → `{t('cancel')}` - `Save & Resend` → `{t('saveResend')}` - `Answer` (two places, the segment label) → `{t('answer')}` - `Thinking...` (two places) → `{t('thinking')}` ### 7. ResultsTable.tsx (`frontend/src/components/ResultsTable.tsx`) Replace: - `placeholder="Search all columns…"` → `placeholder={t('searchColumns')}` - The summary section (lines 109-113): ```tsx // Old: {isFiltered ? `${sortedRows.length} of ${result.rowCount} rows` : `${result.rowCount} row${result.rowCount !== 1 ? 's' : ''}`}{' '} in {result.executionTimeMs.toFixed(1)} ms {truncated && ` (showing first ${DISPLAY_CAP})`} // New: {isFiltered ? t('rowsFilteredInTime', { count: sortedRows.length, total: result.rowCount, time: result.executionTimeMs.toFixed(1) }) : t('rowCountInTime', { count: result.rowCount, time: result.executionTimeMs.toFixed(1) })} {truncated && ` ${t('showingFirst', { count: DISPLAY_CAP })}`} ``` - `placeholder="Filter…"` → `placeholder={t('filterPlaceholder')}` ### 8. InlineQueryResult.tsx (`frontend/src/components/InlineQueryResult.tsx`) The `getToolDisplayName` function needs `t` as a parameter: ```typescript function getToolDisplayName(result: ToolCallResult, t: (key: string) => string): string { const name = result.toolName || ''; if (name.includes('execute_sql')) return t('sqlQuery'); if (name === 'Bash') return t('bash'); if (name === 'Read') return t('readFile'); if (name === 'Write') return t('writeFile'); if (name === 'Edit') return t('editFile'); if (name.startsWith('mcp__')) { const parts = name.split('__'); return parts[parts.length - 1] || name; } return name || 'Tool'; } ``` In `InlineQueryResult`: - Add `const { t } = useTranslation();` - Update call: `const displayName = getToolDisplayName(result, t);` - The meta line with row count: `{result.rowCount} row{result.rowCount !== 1 ? 's' : ''}` → `{t('rowCount', { count: result.rowCount })}` - The showing count: `` {result.rowCount > MAX_DISPLAY_ROWS && ` (showing ${MAX_DISPLAY_ROWS})`} `` → `{result.rowCount > MAX_DISPLAY_ROWS && ` ${t('showingCount', { count: MAX_DISPLAY_ROWS })}`}` - `
Executing...
` → `
{t('executing')}
` ### 9. ResultMarkdown.tsx (`frontend/src/components/ResultMarkdown.tsx`) Replace: - The summary line: `{result.rowCount} row{result.rowCount !== 1 ? 's' : ''} in{' '}{result.executionTimeMs.toFixed(1)} ms` → `{t('rowCountInTime', { count: result.rowCount, time: result.executionTimeMs.toFixed(1) })}` ## Your Job 1. Read each file 2. Make all the replacements listed above 3. Be thorough - don't miss any hardcoded strings 4. Commit all changes together with message: `feat(i18n): translate all UI components to use i18n system` Work from: /Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent

You are implementing Tasks 5-13: Translate all 9 components to use the i18n system. ## Context The i18n system is already set up: - `frontend/src/LanguageContext.tsx` exports `useTranslation()` which returns `{ language, setLanguage, t }` - `t(key)` returns the translated string, `t(key, { param: value })` supports interpolation - Translation files are at `frontend/src/i18n/en.json` and `frontend/src/i18n/zh-TW.json` Your job is to replace ALL hardcoded English strings in each component with `t('key')` calls. For each component: 1. Add `import { useTranslation } from '../LanguageContext';` 2. Add `const { t } = useTranslation();` inside the component function 3. Replace every hardcoded string with the appropriate `t()` call ## Available translation keys (from en.json): ``` appTitle, editorMode, agentMode, switchToLight, switchToDark, switchToZh, switchToEn, connectingToBackend, failedToConnect, uploadDropText, uploadOr, loadSample, loading, uploading, csvOnly, fileTooLarge, queryPlaceholder, runQuery, running, tablesHeader, noTables, expandSidebar, collapseSidebar, deleteTable, deleteTableConfirm, rowCount, agentHeader, langfuseTraces, openLangfuse, langfuseNotConfigured, clear, agentEmptyState, chatPlaceholderWaiting, chatPlaceholder, send, you, assistant, thinking, thinkingLabel, answer, deleteConfirm, delete, cancel, editMessage, deleteMessage, saveResend, searchColumns, filterPlaceholder, rowsOf, showingFirst, sqlQuery, bash, readFile, writeFile, editFile, executing, rowCountInTime, rowsFilteredInTime, showingCount ``` ## Component-by-component instructions: ### 1. FileUpload.tsx (`frontend/src/components/FileUpload.tsx`) Replace: - `alert('Only .csv files are supported.');` → `alert(t('csvOnly'));` - `alert('File exceeds 500MB limit.');` → `alert(t('fileTooLarge'));` - `

Uploading...

` → `

{t('uploading')}

` - `Drop a CSV file here or click to browse` → `{t('uploadDropText')}` - `or` → `{t('uploadOr')}` - `{loadingSample ? 'Loading...' : 'Load Sample Dataset (Titanic)'}` → `{loadingSample ? t('loading') : t('loadSample')}` ### 2. QueryEditor.tsx (`frontend/src/components/QueryEditor.tsx`) Replace: - `placeholder="Enter SQL query... (Ctrl+Enter to run)"` → `placeholder={t('queryPlaceholder')}` - `{running ? 'Running...' : 'Run Query'}` → `{running ? t('running') : t('runQuery')}` ### 3. Sidebar.tsx (`frontend/src/components/Sidebar.tsx`) Replace: - `

Tables

` → `

{t('tablesHeader')}

` - `aria-label={collapsed ? 'Expand sidebar' : 'Collapse sidebar'}` → `aria-label={collapsed ? t('expandSidebar') : t('collapseSidebar')}` - `No tables yet. Upload a CSV to get started.` → `{t('noTables')}` - `{table.rowCount} row{table.rowCount !== 1 ? 's' : ''}` → `{t('rowCount', { count: table.rowCount })}` - `` title={`Delete table "${table.name}"`} `` → `title={t('deleteTable', { name: table.name })}` - `` aria-label={`Delete table ${table.name}`} `` → `aria-label={t('deleteTable', { name: table.name })}` ### 4. AgentPanel.tsx (`frontend/src/components/AgentPanel.tsx`) Replace: - `Agent Mode` → `{t('agentHeader')}` - `title={langfuseStatus.enabled ? 'Open Langfuse dashboard' : 'Langfuse not configured'}` → `title={langfuseStatus.enabled ? t('openLangfuse') : t('langfuseNotConfigured')}` - `Langfuse Traces` → `{t('langfuseTraces')}` - `Clear` → `{t('clear')}` - The empty state text `Ask a question about your data...` → `{t('agentEmptyState')}` ### 5. ChatInput.tsx (`frontend/src/components/ChatInput.tsx`) Replace: - `placeholder={isStreaming ? 'Waiting for response...' : 'Ask about your data...'}` → `placeholder={isStreaming ? t('chatPlaceholderWaiting') : t('chatPlaceholder')}` - `Send` → `{t('send')}` ### 6. MessageBubble.tsx (`frontend/src/components/MessageBubble.tsx`) This one is more complex. Both `ThinkingBlock` and `MessageBubble` need `useTranslation`. For the standalone function `getLastThinkingLine`, it returns `'Thinking...'` as a fallback. Change its signature to accept a `t` parameter: ```typescript function getLastThinkingLine(segments: ContentSegment[], streamingRemainder: string | undefined, t: (key: string) => string): string { ``` And change the last `return 'Thinking...';` to `return t('thinking');` In `ThinkingBlock`: - Add `const { t } = useTranslation();` - Update the call: `const summary = getLastThinkingLine(segments, streamingRemainder, t);` - `Thinking` → `{t('thinkingLabel')}` In `MessageBubble`: - Add `const { t } = useTranslation();` - `{isUser ? 'You' : 'Assistant'}` → `{isUser ? t('you') : t('assistant')}` - `title="Edit message"` → `title={t('editMessage')}` - `title="Delete message"` → `title={t('deleteMessage')}` - `Delete this and all following messages?` → `{t('deleteConfirm')}` - The delete confirm button `Delete` → `{t('delete')}` - The cancel button `Cancel` (two places) → `{t('cancel')}` - `Save & Resend` → `{t('saveResend')}` - `Answer` (two places, the segment label) → `{t('answer')}` - `Thinking...` (two places) → `{t('thinking')}` ### 7. 's' : ''}`}{' '} in {result.executionTimeMs.toFixed(1)} ms {truncated && ` (showing first ${DISPLAY_CAP})`} // New: {isFiltered ? t('rowsFilteredInTime', { count: sortedRows.length, total: result.rowCount, time: result.executionTimeMs.toFixed(1) }) : t('rowCountInTime', { count: result.rowCount, time: result.executionTimeMs.toFixed(1) })} {truncated && ` ${t('showingFirst', { count: DISPLAY_CAP })}`} ``` - `placeholder="Filter…"` → `placeholder={t('filterPlaceholder')}` ### 8. InlineQueryResult.tsx (`frontend/src/components/InlineQueryResult.tsx`) The `getToolDisplayName` function needs `t` as a parameter: ```typescript function getToolDisplayName(result: ToolCallResult, t: (key: string) => string): string { const name = result.toolName || ''; if (name.includes('execute_sql')) return t('sqlQuery'); if (name === 'Bash') return t('bash'); if (name === 'Read') return t('readFile'); if (name === 'Write') return t('writeFile'); if (name === 'Edit') return t('editFile'); if (name.startsWith('mcp__')) { const parts = name.split('__'); return parts[parts.length - 1] || name; } return name || 'Tool'; } ``` In `InlineQueryResult`: - Add `const { t } = useTranslation();` - Update call: `const displayName = getToolDisplayName(result, t);` - The meta line with row count: `{result.rowCount} row{result.rowCount !== 1 ? 's' : ''}` → `{t('rowCount', { count: result.rowCount })}` - The showing count: `` {result.rowCount > MAX_DISPLAY_ROWS && ` (showing ${MAX_DISPLAY_ROWS})`} `` → `{result.rowCount > MAX_DISPLAY_ROWS && ` ${t('showingCount', { count: MAX_DISPLAY_ROWS })}`}` - `
Executing...
` → `
{t('executing')}
` ### 9. ResultMarkdown.tsx (`frontend/src/components/ResultMarkdown.tsx`) Replace: - The summary line: `{result.rowCount} row{result.rowCount !== 1 ? 's' : ''} in{' '}{result.executionTimeMs.toFixed(1)} ms` → `{t('rowCountInTime', { count: result.rowCount, time: result.executionTimeMs.toFixed(1) })}` ## Your Job 1. Read each file 2. Make all the replacements listed above 3. Be thorough - don't miss any hardcoded strings 4. Commit all changes together with message: `feat(i18n): translate all UI components to use i18n system` Work from: /Users/cyyeh/Desktop/duckdb-data-agent

For each component: 1. Add `import { useTranslation } from '../LanguageContext';` 2. Add `const { t } = useTranslation();` inside the component function 3. FileUpload.tsx (`frontend/src/components/FileUpload.tsx`) Replace: - `alert('Only .csv files are supported.');` → `alert(t('csvOnly'));` - `alert('File exceeds 500MB limit.');` → `alert(t('fileTooLarge'));` - `

Uploading...

` → `

{t('uploading')}

` - `Drop a CSV file here or click to browse` → `{t('uploadDropText')}` - `or` → `{t('uploadOr')}` - `{loadingSample ? 'Loading...' : 'Load Sample Dataset (Titanic)'}` → `{loadingSample ? t('loading') : t('loadSample')}` ### 2. QueryEditor.tsx (`frontend/src/components/QueryEditor.tsx`) Replace: - `placeholder="Enter SQL query... (Ctrl+Enter to run)"` → `placeholder={t('queryPlaceholder')}` - `{running ? 'Running...' : 'Run Query'}` → `{running ? t('running') : t('runQuery')}` ### 3. Sidebar.tsx (`frontend/src/components/Sidebar.tsx`) Replace: - `

Tables

{t('tablesHeader')}

Executing...
` → `
{t('executing')}
` ### 9. ResultMarkdown.tsx (`frontend/src/components/ResultMarkdown.tsx`) Replace: - The summary line: `{result.rowCount} row{result.rowCount !== 1 ? 's' : ''} in{' '}{result.executionTimeMs.toFixed(1)} ms` → `{t('rowCountInTime', { count: result.rowCount, time: result.executionTimeMs.toFixed(1) })}` ## Your Job 1. Read each file 2. For each component: 1. Add `import { useTranslation } from '../LanguageContext';` 2. Add `const { t } = useTranslation();` inside the component function 3. Replace every hardcoded string with the appropriate `t()` call ## Available translation keys (from en.json): ``` appTitle, editorMode, agentMode, switchToLight, switchToDark, switchToZh, switchToEn, connectingToBackend, failedToConnect, uploadDropText, uploadOr, loadSample, loading, uploading, csvOnly, fileTooLarge, queryPlaceholder, runQuery, running, tablesHeader, noTables, expandSidebar, collapseSidebar, deleteTable, deleteTableConfirm, rowCount, agentHeader, langfuseTraces, openLangfuse, langfuseNotConfigured, clear, agentEmptyState, chatPlaceholderWaiting, chatPlaceholder, send, you, assistant, thinking, thinkingLabel, answer, deleteConfirm, delete, cancel, editMessage, deleteMessage, saveResend, searchColumns, filterPlaceholder, rowsOf, showingFirst, sqlQuery, bash, readFile, writeFile, editFile, executing, rowCountInTime, rowsFilteredInTime, showingCount ``` ## Component-by-component instructions: ### 1. FileUpload.tsx (`frontend/src/components/FileUpload.tsx`) Replace: - `alert('Only .csv files are supported.');` → `alert(t('csvOnly'));` - `alert('File exceeds 500MB limit.');` → `alert(t('fileTooLarge'));` - `

Uploading...

` → `

{t('uploading')}

` - `Drop a CSV file here or click to browse` → `{t('uploadDropText')}` - `or` → `{t('uploadOr')}` - `{loadingSample ? 'Loading...' : 'Load Sample Dataset (Titanic)'}` → `{loadingSample ? t('loading') : t('loadSample')}` ### 2. QueryEditor.tsx (`frontend/src/components/QueryEditor.tsx`) Replace: - `placeholder="Enter SQL query... (Ctrl+Enter to run)"` → `placeholder={t('queryPlaceholder')}` - `{running ? 'Running...' : 'Run Query'}` → `{running ? t('running') : t('runQuery')}` ### 3. Sidebar.tsx (`frontend/src/components/Sidebar.tsx`) Replace: - `

Tables

` → `

{t('tablesHeader')}

` - `aria-label={collapsed ? 'Expand sidebar' : 'Collapse sidebar'}` → `aria-label={collapsed ? t('expandSidebar') : t('collapseSidebar')}` - `No tables yet. Upload a CSV to get started.` → `{t('noTables')}` - `{table.rowCount} row{table.rowCount !== 1 ? 's' : ''}` → `{t('rowCount', { count: table.rowCount })}` - `` title={`Delete table "${table.name}"`} `` → `title={t('deleteTable', { name: table.name })}` - `` aria-label={`Delete table ${table.name}`} `` → `aria-label={t('deleteTable', { name: table.name })}` ### 4. AgentPanel.tsx (`frontend/src/components/AgentPanel.tsx`) Replace: - `Agent Mode` → `{t('agentHeader')}` - `title={langfuseStatus.enabled ? 'Open Langfuse dashboard' : 'Langfuse not configured'}` → `title={langfuseStatus.enabled ? t('openLangfuse') : t('langfuseNotConfigured')}` - `Langfuse Traces` → `{t('langfuseTraces')}` - `Clear` → `{t('clear')}` - The empty state text `Ask a question about your data...` → `{t('agentEmptyState')}` ### 5. ChatInput.tsx (`frontend/src/components/ChatInput.tsx`) Replace: - `placeholder={isStreaming ? 'Waiting for response...' : 'Ask about your data...'}` → `placeholder={isStreaming ? t('chatPlaceholderWaiting') : t('chatPlaceholder')}` - `Send` → `{t('send')}` ### 6. For the standalone function `getLastThinkingLine`, it returns `'Thinking...'` as a fallback. Change its signature to accept a `t` parameter: ```typescript function getLastThinkingLine(segments: ContentSegment[], streamingRemainder: string | undefined, t: (key: string) => string): string { ``` And change the last `return 'Thinking...';` to `return t('thinking');` In `ThinkingBlock`: - Add `const { t } = useTranslation();` - Update the call: `const summary = getLastThinkingLine(segments, streamingRemainder, t);` - `Thinking` → `{t('thinkingLabel')}` In `MessageBubble`: - Add `const { t } = useTranslation();` - `{isUser ? Executing...
` → `
{t('executing')}
` ### 9. ResultMarkdown.tsx (`frontend/src/components/ResultMarkdown.tsx`) Replace: - The summary line: `{result.rowCount} row{result.rowCount !== 1 ? 's' : ''} in{' '}{result.executionTimeMs.toFixed(1)} ms` → `{t('rowCountInTime', { count: result.rowCount, time: result.executionTimeMs.toFixed(1) })}` ## Your Job 1. Read each file 2. You are implementing Tasks 5-13: Translate all 9 components to use the i18n system. ## Context The i18n system is already set up: - `frontend/src/LanguageContext.tsx` exports `useTranslation()` which returns `{ language, setLanguage, t }` - `t(key)` returns the translated string, `t(key, { param: value })` supports interpolation - Translation files are at `frontend/src/i18n/en.json` and `frontend/src/i18n/zh-TW.json` Your job is to replace ALL hardcoded English strings in each component with `t('key')` calls. For each component: 1. Add `import { useTranslation } from '../LanguageContext';` 2. Add `const { t } = useTranslation();` inside the component function 3. Replace every hardcoded string with the appropriate `t()` call ## Available translation keys (from en.json): ``` appTitle, editorMode, agentMode, switchToLight, switchToDark, switchToZh, switchToEn, connectingToBackend, failedToConnect, uploadDropText, uploadOr, loadSample, loading, uploading, csvOnly, fileTooLarge, queryPlaceholder, runQuery, running, tablesHeader, noTables, expandSidebar, collapseSidebar, deleteTable, deleteTableConfirm, rowCount, agentHeader, langfuseTraces, openLangfuse, langfuseNotConfigured, clear, agentEmptyState, chatPlaceholderWaiting, chatPlaceholder, send, you, assistant, thinking, thinkingLabel, answer, deleteConfirm, delete, cancel, editMessage, deleteMessage, saveResend, searchColumns, filterPlaceholder, rowsOf, showingFirst, sqlQuery, bash, readFile, writeFile, editFile, executing, rowCountInTime, rowsFilteredInTime, showingCount ``` ## Component-by-component instructions: ### 1. FileUpload.tsx (`frontend/src/components/FileUpload.tsx`) Replace: - `alert('Only .csv files are supported.');` → `alert(t('csvOnly'));` - `alert('File exceeds 500MB limit.');` → `alert(t('fileTooLarge'));` - `

Uploading...

` → `

{t('uploading')}

` - `Drop a CSV file here or click to browse` → `{t('uploadDropText')}` - `or` → `{t('uploadOr')}` - `{loadingSample ? 'Loading...' : 'Load Sample Dataset (Titanic)'}` → `{loadingSample ? t('loading') : t('loadSample')}` ### 2. QueryEditor.tsx (`frontend/src/components/QueryEditor.tsx`) Replace: - `placeholder="Enter SQL query... (Ctrl+Enter to run)"` → `placeholder={t('queryPlaceholder')}` - `{running ? 'Running...' : 'Run Query'}` → `{running ? t('running') : t('runQuery')}` ### 3. Sidebar.tsx (`frontend/src/components/Sidebar.tsx`) Replace: - `

Tables

` → `

{t('tablesHeader')}

` - `aria-label={collapsed ? 'Expand sidebar' : 'Collapse sidebar'}` → `aria-label={collapsed ? t('expandSidebar') : t('collapseSidebar')}` - `No tables yet. Upload a CSV to get started.` → `{t('noTables')}` - `{table.rowCount} row{table.rowCount !== 1 ? 's' : ''}` → `{t('rowCount', { count: table.rowCount })}` - `` title={`Delete table "${table.name}"`} `` → `title={t('deleteTable', { name: table.name })}` - `` aria-label={`Delete table ${table.name}`} `` → `aria-label={t('deleteTable', { name: table.name })}` ### 4. AgentPanel.tsx (`frontend/src/components/AgentPanel.tsx`) Replace: - `Agent Mode` → `{t('agentHeader')}` - `title={langfuseStatus.enabled ? 'Open Langfuse dashboard' : 'Langfuse not configured'}` → `title={langfuseStatus.enabled ? t('openLangfuse') : t('langfuseNotConfigured')}` - `Langfuse Traces` → `{t('langfuseTraces')}` - `Clear` → `{t('clear')}` - The empty state text `Ask a question about your data...` → `{t('agentEmptyState')}` ### 5. 'Waiting for response...' : 'Ask about your data...'}` → `placeholder={isStreaming ? t('chatPlaceholderWaiting') : t('chatPlaceholder')}` - `Send` → `{t('send')}` ### 6. 's' : ''}` → `{t('rowCount', { count: result.rowCount })}` - The showing count: `` {result.rowCount > MAX_DISPLAY_ROWS && ` (showing ${MAX_DISPLAY_ROWS})`} `` → `{result.rowCount > MAX_DISPLAY_ROWS && ` ${t('showingCount', { count: MAX_DISPLAY_ROWS })}`}` - `
Executing...
` → `
{t('executing')}
` ### 9. ResultMarkdown.tsx (`frontend/src/components/ResultMarkdown.tsx`) Replace: - The summary line: `{result.rowCount} row{result.rowCount !== 1 ? 's' : ''} in{' '}{result.executionTimeMs.toFixed(1)} ms` → `{t('rowCountInTime', { count: result.rowCount, time: result.executionTimeMs.toFixed(1) })}` ## Your Job 1. Read each file 2. content.content:
1→# i18n Design: English + Traditional Chinese
     2→
     3→**Date:** 2026-02-20
     4→**Scope:** Frontend UI strings only (not AI agent responses)
     5→**Languages:** English (`en`), Traditional Chinese (`zh-TW`)
     6→
     7→## Approach
     8→
     9→Custom React Context + JSON translation files. Zero new dependencies. Mirrors the existing `ThemeContext` pattern.
    10→
    11→## Architecture
    12→
    13→### New Files
    14→
    15→- `frontend/src/i18n/en.json` — English translation strings
    16→- `frontend/src/i18n/zh-TW.json` — Traditional Chinese translation strings
    17→- `frontend/src/LanguageContext.tsx` — Language state, provider, and `useTranslation` hook
    18→
    19→### Modified Files
    20→
    21→- `frontend/src/App.tsx` — Wrap with `LanguageProvider`, add language toggle in header
    22→- All component files — Replace hardcoded strings with `t('key')` calls
    23→
    24→### Language Detection Priority
    25→
    26→1. `localStorage.getItem('language')` (user's saved preference)
    27→2. `navigator.language` — if starts with `zh`, use `zh-TW`; otherwise `en`
    28→3. Fallback: `en`
    29→
    30→### LanguageContext API
    31→
    32→```typescript
    33→type Language = 'en' | 'zh-TW';
    34→
    35→interface LanguageContextType {
    36→  language: Language;
    37→  setLanguage: (lang: Language) => void;
    38→  t: (key: string, params?: Record<string, string | number>) => string;
    39→}
    40→```
    41→
    42→The `t()` function:
    43→- Looks up the key in the current language's translation file
    44→- Supports simple interpolation: `t('rows', { count: 5 })` replaces `{count}` in the string
    45→- Falls back to returning the key itself if not found
    46→
    47→## UI Toggle
    48→
    49→- **Position:** Header, immediately left of the sun/moon theme toggle
    50→- **Style:** Same button styling as theme toggle
    51→- **Label:** Shows `EN` when in English, `中` when in Traditional Chinese
    52→- **Behavior:** Click toggles between the two languages
    53→- **Accessibility:** `aria-label` of "Switch to 中文" / "Switch to English"
    54→
    55→## Translation Keys
    56→
    57→~40 flat key-value pairs covering: app title, mode labels, upload text, query editor placeholders, sidebar labels, agent panel text, chat input, message bubbles, results table, tool names, confirmation dialogs, error messages.
    58→
    59→Both language files use identical keys.
    60→
    61→## Data Flow
    62→
    63→```
    64→User clicks toggle → setLanguage('zh-TW') → localStorage updated
    65→→ LanguageContext re-renders → all t() calls return new language strings
    66→→ UI updates instantly (no page reload)
    67→→ document.documentElement.lang updated for accessibility
    68→```
    69→
    70→## Edge Cases
    71→
    72→- **Invalid localStorage value:** Falls back to OS detection, then `en`
    73→- **OS language not zh or en:** Defaults to `en`
    74→- **Missing translation key:** Returns the key itself (non-breaking fallback)
    75→- **HTML `lang` attribute:** Updated on `<html>` element when language changes
    76→
    77→## Out of Scope (YAGNI)
    78→
    79→- RTL support (neither language needs it)
    80→- Number/date formatting (app uses raw SQL output)
    81→- Plural rules (using `{count} row(s)` pattern)
    82→- Namespacing (only ~40 keys)
    83→- Lazy loading of translations (files are tiny)
    84→- Backend/agent translation (excluded per design decision)
    85→

1→# DuckDB Data Agent
     2→
     3→> **Note:** This project is built with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code)(using Opus 4.6 and [superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers)) by more than 95% and human-reviewed by author.
     4→
     5→[![Deploy to Render](https://render.com/images/deploy-to-render-button.svg)](https://render.com/deploy)
     6→
     7→A SQL playground with an AI-powered data analysis agent. Upload CSV files, write SQL queries, or ask questions in plain English — powered by [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) on a lightweight [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) backend with a React frontend.
     8→
     9→## Features
    10→
    11→### General
    12→
    13→- **Dark / light mode** — Toggle between dark and light themes with the sun/moon button in the header; respects your OS preference on first visit and remembers your choice across sessions
    14→
    15→### SQL Playground
    16→
    17→- **DuckDB SQL engine** — Fast, in-process analytical database on the backend
    18→- **CSV file upload** — Drag-and-drop or click to import CSV files (up to 500 MB) with automatic schema detection
    19→- **Sample dataset** — One-click load of the Titanic dataset to get started quickly
    20→- **SQL query editor** — Write and execute queries with Ctrl/Cmd+Enter
    21→- **Interactive results** — Sortable columns, per-column filters, and global search across results
    22→- **EXPLAIN support** — Markdown-rendered output for `EXPLAIN` and `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` queries
    23→- **Table sidebar** — Collapsible panel to browse tables, inspect columns, and view types
    24→
    25→### AI Agent
    26→
    27→- **Natural language queries** — Ask questions about your data in plain English; the agent writes and executes SQL for you
    28→- **Streaming responses** — Real-time token streaming powered by Claude via the [Anthropic Agent SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python)
    29→- **Visible reasoning** — Collapsible thinking block shows the agent's intermediate steps and SQL queries
    30→- **Inline results** — Query results rendered inline within the conversation
    31→- **Edit & delete messages** — Hover over any user message to edit or delete it; editing re-sends the modified query with prior conversation as context, deleting rewinds the conversation to that point
    32→- **Privacy-conscious** — Requires an Anthropic API key stored in a server-side `.env` file; your data and key are never sent anywhere besides the Anthropic API
    33→- **Langfuse observability** (optional) — Built-in [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/) tracing for monitoring agent interactions, with a one-click dashboard link in the UI
    34→
    35→## Getting Started
    36→
    37→### Prerequisites
    38→
    39→- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 20+
    40→- [Python](https://www.python.org/) 3.12+
    41→- [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/)
    42→
    43→### Installation
    44→
    45→```bash
    46→make install
    47→```
    48→
    49→Or install frontend and backend separately:
    50→
    51→```bash
    52→cd frontend && npm install
    53→cd backend && poetry install
    54→```
    55→

# DuckDB Data Agent

> **Note:** This project is built with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code)(using Opus 4.6 and [superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers)) by more than 95% and human-reviewed by author.

[![Deploy to Render](https://render.com/images/deploy-to-render-button.svg)](https://render.com/deploy)

A SQL playground with an AI-powered data analysis agent. Upload CSV files, write SQL queries, or ask questions in plain English — powered by [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) on a lightweight [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) backend with a React frontend.

## Features

### General

- **Dark / light mode** — Toggle between dark and light themes with the sun/moon button in the header; respects your OS preference on first visit and remembers your choice across sessions

### SQL Playground

- **DuckDB SQL engine** — Fast, in-process analytical database on the backend
- **CSV file upload** — Drag-and-drop or click to import CSV files (up to 500 MB) with automatic schema detection
- **Sample dataset** — One-click load of the Titanic dataset to get started quickly
- **SQL query editor** — Write and execute queries with Ctrl/Cmd+Enter
- **Interactive results** — Sortable columns, per-column filters, and global search across results
- **EXPLAIN support** — Markdown-rendered output for `EXPLAIN` and `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` queries
- **Table sidebar** — Collapsible panel to browse tables, inspect columns, and view types

### AI Agent

- **Natural language queries** — Ask questions about your data in plain English; the agent writes and executes SQL for you
- **Streaming responses** — Real-time token streaming powered by Claude via the [Anthropic Agent SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python)
- **Visible reasoning** — Collapsible thinking block shows the agent's intermediate steps and SQL queries
- **Inline results** — Query results rendered inline within the conversation
- **Edit & delete messages** — Hover over any user message to edit or delete it; editing re-sends the modified query with prior conversation as context, deleting rewinds the conversation to that point
- **Privacy-conscious** — Requires an Anthropic API key stored in a server-side `.env` file; your data and key are never sent anywhere besides the Anthropic API
- **Langfuse observability** (optional) — Built-in [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/) tracing for monitoring agent interactions, with a one-click dashboard link in the UI

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 20+
- [Python](https://www.python.org/) 3.12+
- [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/)

### Installation

```bash
make install
```

Or install frontend and backend separately:

```bash
cd frontend && npm install
cd backend && poetry install
```

### Configuration

Copy the example environment file and add your Anthropic API key:

```bash
cp backend/.env.example backend/.env
```

Edit `backend/.env` and set your key:

```
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
ANTHROPIC_MODEL=sonnet    # optional, defaults to sonnet
```

> Both variables are only needed for the AI agent. The SQL playground works without them, but both require the backend running.

#### Langfuse (optional)

To enable agent tracing with [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/), add these to `backend/.env`:

```
LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-...
LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-...
LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com   # optional, defaults to cloud
```

When configured, every agent conversation is traced (LLM turns, tool calls, SQL execution) and a **Langfuse Traces** button appears in the agent panel header linking to your dashboard. When not configured, tracing is disabled with zero overhead.

### Development

Start both the frontend and backend:

```bash
make dev
```

Or run them separately:

```bash
make frontend   # http://localhost:5173
make backend    # http://localhost:8000
```

Open http://localhost:5173 to use the app. The Vite dev server proxies `/api` requests to the backend automatically.

## Production Build and Deployment

The project ships as a single Docker image that bundles the React frontend and FastAPI backend. A multi-stage `Dockerfile` builds the frontend, then copies the output into the backend's static directory.

### Build and run locally

```bash
docker build -t duckdb-data-agent .
docker run -p 10000:10000 \
  -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... \
  -e LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-... \
  -e LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-... \
  duckdb-data-agent
```

Open http://localhost:10000 to use the app.

### Deploy to Render

A `render.yaml` is included for one-click deployment on [Render](https://render.com/):

1. Push this repo to GitHub.
2. In Render, create a new **Blueprint** and connect the repo.
3. Set the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable in the Render dashboard. Optionally set `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` to override the default model (`sonnet`). To enable Langfuse tracing, also set `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY` and `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY`.

Render will build the Docker image and deploy it automatically on every push to `main`.

## Project Structure

```
├── frontend/               # React frontend
│   ├── public/             #   Static assets (Langfuse icon)
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── components/     #   UI components (editor, results, sidebar, chat)
│   │   ├── agent/          #   Agent service (SSE event handling)
│   │   ├── AgentContext.tsx #   Agent state management
│   │   ├── ThemeContext.tsx #   Dark/light theme state & persistence
│   │   └── types.ts        #   Shared TypeScript interfaces
│   ├── index.html          #   HTML entry point
│   ├── package.json        #   npm config
│   └── vite.config.ts      #   Vite bundler config
├── backend/                # FastAPI backend
│   └── app/
│       ├── main.py         #   App setup & CORS
│       ├── config.py       #   Environment variables (API key, model)
│       ├── database.py     #   DuckDB connection & query execution
│       ├── agent.py        #   Agent loop & SSE streaming
│       ├── tracing.py      #   Langfuse client wrapper & initialization
│       ├── tools.py        #   Agent SDK tool definitions (execute_sql)
│       ├── data/           #   Sample datasets (titanic.csv)
│       └── routes/         #   API endpoints (tables, query, chat, langfuse status)
├── Dockerfile              # Multi-stage production build
├── render.yaml             # Render deployment config
└── Makefile                # Dev commands (install, dev, clean)
```

## Tech Stack

**Frontend**
- [React](https://react.dev/) 18 + [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)
- [Vite](https://vite.dev/)

**Backend**
- [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) + [Uvicorn](https://www.uvicorn.org/)
- [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) (Python)
- [Anthropic Agent SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python)
- [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/) (optional, for observability)

## License

[MIT](LICENSE.txt)

  -e LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-... \
  -e LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-... \
  duckdb-data-agent
```

Open http://localhost:10000 to use the app.

### Deploy to Render

A `render.yaml` is included for one-click deployment on [Render](https://render.com/):

1. Push this repo to GitHub.
2. In Render, create a new **Blueprint** and connect the repo.
3. Set the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable in the Render dashboard. Optionally set `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` to override the default model (`sonnet`). To enable Langfuse tracing, also set `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY` and `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY`.

Render will build the Docker image and deploy it automatically on every push to `main`.

## Project Structure

```
├── frontend/               # React frontend
│   ├── public/             #   Static assets (Langfuse icon)
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── components/     #   UI components (editor, results, sidebar, chat)
│   │   ├── agent/          #   Agent service (SSE event handling)
│   │   ├── AgentContext.tsx #   Agent state management
│   │   ├── ThemeContext.tsx #   Dark/light theme state & persistence
│   │   └── types.ts        #   Shared TypeScript interfaces
│   ├── index.html          #   HTML entry point
│   ├── package.json        #   npm config
│   └── vite.config.ts      #   Vite bundler config
├── backend/                # FastAPI backend
│   └── app/
│       ├── main.py         #   App setup & CORS
│       ├── config.py       #   Environment variables (API key, model)
│       ├── database.py     #   DuckDB connection & query execution
│       ├── agent.py        #   Agent loop & SSE streaming
│       ├── tracing.py      #   Langfuse client wrapper & initialization
│       ├── tools.py        #   Agent SDK tool definitions (execute_sql)
│       ├── data/           #   Sample datasets (titanic.csv)
│       └── routes/         #   API endpoints (tables, query, chat, langfuse status)
├── Dockerfile              # Multi-stage production build
├── render.yaml             # Render deployment config
└── Makefile                # Dev commands (install, dev, clean)
```

## Tech Stack

**Frontend**
- [React](https://react.dev/) 18 + [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)
- [Vite](https://vite.dev/)

**Backend**
- [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) + [Uvicorn](https://www.uvicorn.org/)
- [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) (Python)
- [Anthropic Agent SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python)
- [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/) (optional, for observability)
